def: The ability to answer new questions about a running system from the data it emits, without shipping new code to find out.
The complete record of one request as it passes through a system, made up of spans.
One timed operation within a trace, with a name, attributes, a parent and a status.
The open standard and set of libraries for emitting traces, metrics and logs and sending them to any compatible backend.
Agreed names for common telemetry attributes, so that different tools describing the same thing use the same key.
OpenTelemetry's naming rules for spans, attributes and metrics of model calls, tool calls and agents, currently in Development status.
Recording the text of prompts, replies and tool arguments on spans; an opt-in choice because the text often contains sensitive data.
Deciding whether to keep a trace when it starts, before anything is known about how it will turn out.
Deciding whether to keep a trace after it has finished, so rules can use errors, latency, scores and feedback.
The inverse of the probability that a trace was kept, used to compute unbiased rates from a non-uniform sample.
Passing trace identifiers across process boundaries so that spans from different services join one trace.
A scorer that runs on sampled production traces to estimate quality continuously.
